en: Points of Controversy Great Chapter Fifteen Sixteenth Section
The Discourse on Bestowing Happiness:
One bestows happiness upon another, does one? Yes.
Does one person inflict suffering upon another?
You should not say so... [and so on] ...
Does one person not inflict suffering upon another?
“Yes,” [you say].
“Then one person does not bestow happiness upon another?
You should not speak thus … [and so on] …
Does one person bestow happiness upon another? Yes.
Does one person bestow his own happiness upon another, bestow the happiness of others, or bestow that [specific] happiness?
It should not be said thus … [as before] … “Another does not bestow happiness upon another, nor upon himself, nor upon others, nor upon that person”?
Yes, it should be so admitted.
If another person does not bestow happiness upon another, nor upon himself, nor upon others, nor upon that very person, then surely it should not be said:
"Another person bestows happiness upon another.
Does another person bestow happiness upon another?
“Yes,” you say.
“One person is the doer for another; one person makes happiness or suffering for another, and another experiences it”?
You should not speak thus… [as before]… No, indeed.
Is it not to be said that one person bestows happiness upon another?
Yes, it is so.
Did not the Venerable Udāyī say this:
“The Blessed One has indeed removed for us many states of suffering; the Blessed One has indeed brought about for us many states of happiness;
the Blessed One has indeed removed for us many unwholesome states; the Blessed One has indeed brought about for us many wholesome states”?
“The Blessed One is the one who brings about the destruction of unwholesome states.
Is this indeed a sutta?
Yes, it is.
Therefore, one person bestows happiness upon another.
The Discussion on the Bestowal of Happiness is finished.
